A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CASS dataset, translation models, pipeline, and benchmark. Their main text and appendices are readable, including tables, plots, and code examples, and permit reliable comparison despite substantial evaluation and presentation revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original translation experiments, data-source ablations, dataset analyses, and runtime/memory measurements in Sections 4–6 and the appendix.

after.justification: V4 reports original benchmark results, ablations, hardware-transfer experiments, failure analyses, and energy measurements in Sections 4–6 and the appendix.

M1.justification: The scraping/synthesis, HIPIFY conversion, assembly extraction, supervised Qwen2.5-Coder fine-tuning, and RoPE extrapolation procedures are retained. Expanded deduplication descriptions and additional hardware configurations do not establish a new translation algorithm, architecture, or objective.

E1.justification: CASS-Bench shifts from Claude-generated implementations to repository-derived programs. Reported coverage expands from 16 to 18 domains, including Utility/System and Device Management. V4 also introduces explicit evaluation of an sm80-trained model on sm89 inputs, extending the hardware conditions tested.

E2.justification: Table 3 replaces the earlier commercial-model comparisons with GPT-5-mini/5.1, Claude-Haiku-4.5, and Gemini-2.5 variants, and adds LLaMA, Gemma, Qwen3, OLMo, and DeepSeek comparators. ZLUDA, Hipify, and Qwen2.5-Coder-32B remain. Earlier GPT-4o qualitative comparisons are retained in Appendix A.8.2.

E3.justification: The benchmark changes from 40 manually checked, Claude-generated samples to 369 repository-derived samples with stated train/test deduplication and automated differential testing. Training-corpus totals and composition are revised. Table 3 adds compilation rate and prediction chrF, while efficiency reporting changes from percentage differences to MB and seconds.

E4.justification: V4 adds hardware-transfer and input-length tests, prompting comparisons, operation-level failure analysis, six assembly-error case studies, and aggregate/model-wise compilation-error breakdowns. The data-source/RoPE ablation and earlier qualitative source-code comparisons remain. V1's per-domain accuracy plot is replaced by failure-oriented analyses.

E5.justification: V4 Table 3 newly includes ± terms for accuracy and compilation rates, without defining their statistical meaning or run/seed basis. Runtime and memory measurements already used 20 executions and uncertainty displays in v1; v4 retains that run count. An increase in repeated runs is not established.

E6.justification: Table 3 replaces CASS-7B's 37.5% assembly and 95% source accuracy with CASS-sm80-7B's 69.11% and 88.17% on the revised benchmark. Table 4's ablation results and training curves also change. New outcomes include 32.5% hardware-transfer accuracy, failure breakdowns, and energy measurements. These are results under changed conditions, not demonstrated same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theoretical results, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations. V4's additional metric descriptions and assembly-error examples are empirical evaluation material rather than new theory.

C1.justification: The four central contributions—dataset, benchmark, models, and construction pipeline—and their novelty positioning remain. Headline claims revise the corpus and benchmark scope, translation accuracies, comparator generations, and native-performance preservation from over 85% to 95%. The preservation claims use different reporting criteria, so they do not establish a directly comparable improvement.

C2.justification: V4 adds substantive explanations involving ISA encoding constraints, limited pretraining exposure, long-context degradation, hardware-generation differences, and learning beyond Hipify's substitutions. Its limitations section newly specifies Tensor Core, WMMA, and HIPIFY coverage gaps. Earlier architecture and context limitations receive expanded discussion and experiments elsewhere rather than simply disappearing.

D1.justification: V4 adds baseline prompts and default-decoding information, prompt/AST/opcode deduplication details, and the two-epoch CodeCarbon measurement setup. Existing fine-tuning hyperparameters, hardware descriptions, and synthetic prompt templates largely remain. The repository link changes, while release wording becomes inconsistent: the abstract promises future release but the conclusion states resources are released.

R1.justification: V4 adds references for newer comparison models, SASS decoding, GPU architecture documentation, and long-context limitations. The central positioning against source/IR translators, CPU transpilation approaches, and GPU datasets without aligned assembly remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and results narrative are substantially rewritten, related-work subsections become compact topical paragraphs, and efficiency/similarity discussion moves into Results. CASS-Instruct terminology is simplified, the conclusion precedes limitations, and the appendix is extensively reorganized. A language-model-use disclosure is also added.

P2.justification: V4 adopts a two-column layout, expands Table 3 into grouped model families and multiple metrics, and recomposes the coverage figure. It adds runtime-distribution, length-sensitivity, and error-analysis plots, redraws profiling and training curves, and removes the opcode word clouds. These are substantial display changes beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: V4 substantially strengthens v1's limited empirical validation through repository-derived evaluation, broader comparators, separate compilation and correctness measurements, and explicit hardware/length failure tests. Concrete assembly-error examples also clarify applicability limits. Undefined ± statistics, unreconciled corpus counts, and some discrepancies between error-analysis prose and figures remain material weaknesses. Nevertheless, the stronger validation and failure characterization provide substantial overall gains; this judgment does not depend on treating the changed headline accuracies as comparable improvements.
